title: A leap second at the right time of day on the wrong day
why: `2026-01-01T23:59:60Z` reads `23:59` UTC and is still not a leap-second instant: RFC 3339 admits `:60` at the end of a UTC **month**, and 1 January is the start of one. Its sibling `…-off-instant` only moves the *time of day*, so an engine checking the clock and not the calendar passes that case and admits `:60` on 334 days of the year. Month-end is as static as the time of day — no table, nothing to keep current — so both halves are checkable.
